headline: Democrats' gains, a Brampton plant fight and Nvidia's CEO exit mark the week
summary: Democrats added a Mississippi Senate seat to their midterm sweep while hopes for an Iran deal rose and then faded, sending oil back toward US$96. In Ontario, Stellantis's sale of the Brampton plant set off a confrontation with Ottawa, and the province named powerful new regional chairs. Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned after reports of affairs and a suspected Chinese intelligence link.

top.headline: Democrats' Senate majority grows as Colom flips Mississippi
top.what: Democrat Scott Colom was projected the winner over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday and she conceded, adding to the Democratic sweep of both chambers on Nov. 3. Alaska is the last uncalled Senate race.
top.why: Control of Congress changes in January, which affects tariffs, oversight of the White House and U.S. policy toward Canada.

top.headline: Iran hopes fade as Trump says no deal is needed; oil rebounds
top.what: Brent dipped below US$90 on Tuesday on hopes for a deal, then settled at US$95.82 on Thursday after Trump said the U.S. needs no agreement and pulled Vance off the talks. Israel's cabinet reportedly ordered readiness for a strike.
top.why: The war and the Hormuz blockade drive what Ontarians pay for gas and feed the inflation the Bank of Canada is fighting.

top.headline: Stellantis sells Brampton plant; Ottawa serves default notice
top.what: Stellantis said Monday it will sell its idled Brampton assembly plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel. On Thursday Industry Minister Joly ended talks and gave the company 30 days to fix its breach of a 2022 funding deal.
top.why: About 1,800 laid-off Brampton workers and up to $529 million in public subsidies are at stake.

top.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns amid affair and espionage reports
top.what: The co-founder quit as chief executive on Thursday after reports of relationships including one with a suspected Chinese agent; finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO and Huang has agreed to brief Congress.
top.why: Nvidia is among the most widely held stocks in pension and index funds, so its swings reach most retirement savings.

top.headline: Federal budget's $62.3B deficit and immigration plan draw fire
top.what: The Nov. 5 budget projects a $62.3-billion deficit and $142 billion in new spending; by Thursday the fight had moved to its immigration measures, which Poilievre called 'bonkers' and the minister defended as temporary.
top.why: The budget sets federal taxes, spending and immigration levels that shape GTA housing and jobs.

top.headline: Ford government appoints eight regional chairs with 'strong chair' powers
top.what: The province named heads for York, Peel, Durham, Halton and four other regions on Tuesday, including Vaughan Mayor Steven Del Duca in York, prompting objections from Markham's mayor and the ousted Muskoka chair.
top.why: The chairs can veto some bylaws and propose regional budgets that set property taxes and services across the GTA.

top.headline: Ontario moves to cap OSAP at private career colleges
top.what: After a week of student protests and a continuing freeze on aid at career colleges, the province on Thursday outlined a bill to cap OSAP-funded enrolment and bar mostly-online programs.
top.why: Thousands of students are waiting to learn whether and when their aid will resume.

top.headline: Ukraine talks yield prisoner swap but no breakthrough
top.what: Talks in Abu Dhabi produced an agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange, and U.S. envoys met Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy near Dublin on Thursday without a deal on territory or security guarantees.
top.why: A settlement would ease energy and food prices and shape Canada's defence commitments in Europe.
